reference.title: High pressure-high temperature equations of state of neon and diamond

methods.source_location: Final article, sections 2.1 and 3.1, Figure 1 caption, and Table 3 note
methods.notes: Pressures use the Dewaele et al. (2008) Ne Mie-Gruneisen-Debye scale from the measured Ne 111 volume and temperature. Offline ruby fluorescence was secondary verification only.

recalculation.notes: Every paired Ne unit-cell volume, uncertainty, and temperature is bundled, but the exact Dewaele et al. (2008) Ne thermal EOS is not yet an executable Peritheos calibration record.

assessment.basis: Every compared free coefficient meets both the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison and parameter-specific numerical similarity screen. Error conventions and fit qualifications remain applicable.

scientific_validation.note: Validated against the final article, its complete article tables, the corresponding author's machine-readable table mirror, and the author's PVT-tool implementation; LitCurate was discovery-only.

locations: final article, equations 1-11 and Tables 1, 3, and 4

primary_source_check.finding: The executable record is the complete published 300 K Vinet plus integrated constant-q MGD model for the measured 13% Fe composition. It is not a room-temperature slice of the thermal fit.

primary_data_check.finding: All 153 observations are bundled in source order: 49 measurements at 300 K and 104 laser-heated measurements, with reduced pressure and total propagated uncertainty, temperature and uncertainty, bridgmanite cell volume and uncertainty, and paired Ne cell volume and uncertainty.

independent_refit.objective: joint weighted pressure residuals using the final printed total pressure uncertainties, plus the published independent Gaussian priors on V0, gamma0, and q; theta0 fixed to 1000 K
independent_refit.notes: This independently evaluates the rounded published P-V-T table and final effective pressure errors. It reproduces every displayed coefficient within rounding or far inside its 68% interval, but it is not substituted for the authors' iterative marker-volume error-model fit.

unresolved_issues: The publisher record exposes no separate supporting-information file; the final article states that the analyzed data are included in its tables, and the corresponding author supplies exact machine-readable mirrors of Tables 1-5.
The exact Dewaele et al. (2008) Ne thermal pressure scale is identified and all paired calibrant observations are available, but that calibration record is not bundled in Peritheos.
The article does not publish a positional refinement for the exact 13% Fe specimen; diffraction metadata therefore use an explicitly labeled near-composition structural proxy.
The article's equation 13 ideal lattice mixing model for arbitrary Fe content is a separate compositional interpolation and is not represented as another single-composition EOS record.

parameter_provenance.K0: Final article, Table 3, 13% Fe column: fitted K0T=243.8(43) GPa

parameter_provenance.q: Final article, Table 3, 13% Fe column: fitted 0.56(37), with prior 1 +/- 1
parameter_provenance.n: Final article, equation 3 definition CVmax=3 kB Ncell and PVT-tool input natom=20 for the Z=4 cell; exactly equivalent to n=5 per formula unit in Peritheos
parameter_provenance.parameter_covariance: Reconstructed from the 68% parameter errors in final Table 3 and the complete correlation matrix in final Table 4. The V0 row and column are converted from cell-volume units to Peritheos's internal molar-volume unit using N_A*1e-25/Z; all reported correlations are preserved.

superseded_record_text.notes: The 300 K Vinet parameters and thermal parameters are one coupled published thermal EOS. V0, K0, K0', gamma0, and q were fitted; Tr=300 K, theta0=1000 K, and the 20-atom conventional-cell count were fixed. The complete five-parameter covariance is reconstructed from Tables 3-4 rather than treating strongly correlated errors as independent. Table 5 provides an independent source-output check: at 108.7 GPa and 2387 K the implementation reproduces density 5.40 g/cm3, KS=604.5 GPa, gamma=1.23, and Cv/(3Nk)=0.9838 at the source's printed precision.
validity_notes: Marginal envelope of the 153 observations; the sampled P-T paths are not a rectangular phase-stability guarantee.
The authors report that every experimental state followed a thermodynamic path within the bridgmanite stability field and found no H-phase exsolution.
